## Problem 1.1: Heating a water stream

A process heater raises 500 kg/h of liquid water from 20 °C to 80 °C at
constant pressure. Taking the specific heat capacity of water as
$c_p = 4.18\ \text{kJ}\,\text{kg}^{-1}\,\text{K}^{-1}$, determine the heat
duty in kW.

::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions"}
**Solution**

With no phase change and constant $c_p$, the steady-state energy balance
reduces to a sensible-heat term:

$$\dot{Q} = \dot{m}\,c_p\,\Delta T
= (500)(4.18)(80 - 20) = 125{,}400\ \text{kJ/h}.$$

Converting to kW:

$$\dot{Q} = \frac{125{,}400\ \text{kJ/h}}{3600\ \text{s/h}} \approx 34.8\ \text{kW}.$$
:::
